correctness.rationale: In characteristic three F=Q(Q²+Σ X_i^4), and the product of the four linear forms is exactly the parenthesized factor. Direct finite calculation confirms four distinct tangent points and six distinct line-pair intersections off Q, with no triple intersections. At a contact the two split branches glue modulo u², so the completed normalization unit quotient is the unit group of k[u]/(u²), split as G_m times G_a by c(1+du); at a node it is G_m. Component scalars act only on the multiplicative factors and their image is a four-dimensional split subtorus (spanning-tree incidence minor unimodular). Normalized components have trivial Pic^0, so the resulting identity component is G_m^6 times G_a^4 as a group scheme, not merely on rational points. Counting five split rational components and subtracting the ten distinct pairwise intersections gives 5q−5 and the zeta formula; the Picard point count follows from the decomposition. The same four rational sign vectors are the generic nodes: for A=X², B=Y², C=Z², the differences of the derivatives of the cubic in A,B,C are (A−B)[5(A+B)+14C] and cyclic variants. There is no common derivative zero with a zero projective coordinate, with all three squares distinct, or with exactly two equal and the third −19/5 times them. At equal squares the affine quadratic part is nondegenerate. This identifies specialization without using a stable model.
residual_risks: The finite check establishes coefficient and incidence data, not the Picard identity or all-extension formulas independently of the proof. The archived verifier was not executed. No Néron or stable reduction result follows.
